lesson.cantilever.title: Why does it bend? Why is the stress highest there?
lesson.cantilever.body: The bending moment is largest at the fixed end: M(x) = P·(L−x). Top fibres are in tension, bottom in compression; near the neutral axis the stress almost vanishes. Watch the heatmap!
lesson.trussBridge.title: Truss or continuous structure?
lesson.trussBridge.body: Stress is nearly uniform in each member: the top chord is in compression, the bottom in tension, diagonals carry shear. Increase the load and watch where stress grows fastest!
lesson.plateWithHole.title: Stress concentration: the rule of three
lesson.plateWithHole.body: Near a circular hole σmax ≈ 3σ₀ — stress concentrates at the sides of the hole. That is why plates crack at holes and corners! Change the mesh density: on a fine mesh the peak approaches 3σ₀.
